  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains, by analogy to the soul and body, that the ultimate revelation achieved through serving G-d with Torah and mitzvos in a physical body will primarily be at the time of the Resurrection of the Dead, which is far superior even to the highest level of the Garden of Eden.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And along the lines of what is known regarding the matter of soul and body,</t>
    <t s="1">in addition to the fact that the G-dly revelation drawn to the soul through its service in Torah and mitzvos while clothed in a body is a revelation far superior to the revelation it had before its descent below,</t>
    <t s="2">nevertheless, the revelation that comes through the service of Torah and mitzvos in a physical body will primarily be at the time of the Resurrection of the Dead,</t>
    <t s="3">when the soul will be clothed in a physical body.</t>
    <t s="4">For although even the revelation in the Garden of Eden after the soul departs from the body is far superior to the revelation of the Garden of Eden that the soul had before its descent,</t>
    <t s="5">because the revelation of the Garden of Eden after its descent into a body and its departure from the body comes through the service of Torah and mitzvos in a physical body,</t>
    <t s="6">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="7">the primary revelation that comes through the service of Torah and mitzvos will be at the Resurrection of the Dead,</t>
    <t s="8">when the soul will be clothed in a body 52.</t>
    <t s="9">And this is also understood from the matter of the Resurrection of the Dead itself,</t>
    <t s="10">that all of Israel will rise to life,</t>
    <t s="11">even the souls that have been in the Garden of Eden for several thousand years,</t>
    <t s="12">and three times each day they ascend to a more elevated level,</t>
    <t s="13">and nevertheless, in the future they will be clothed in bodies,</t>
    <t s="14">because the revelation of the World of Resurrection is far superior to the revelation of the Garden of Eden, even the most elevated level of the Garden of Eden 53.</t>
  </section>

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the Tzemach Tzedek's notes on Psalm 67 to the Alshich's interpretation that the psalm speaks of the Messianic era, involving both blessing for Israel and sanctification of G-d's name among the nations, and explains the relationship between "mizmor" and "shir" in terms of angelic and soul song, the refinement of the animal soul during the Omer, and the refinement of the nations.

translations.translation: And one can connect this with what the Tzemach Tzedek wrote in his notes on Tehillim 44
regarding the psalm "For the conductor, on melodies, a psalm, a song" 45
(which is recited after the Counting of the Omer 46),
that the Alshich wrote
that this psalm speaks of the days of Mashiach,
when there will be two things.
An abundance of blessings for Israel — "May G-d be gracious to us and bless us" etc. 47,
and His name will be sanctified in the world — "For You will judge the peoples with equity" etc. 48.
And this is that at the beginning of the psalm it says "a psalm, a song,"
"mizmor" regarding the first matter, "shir" regarding the second matter.
And after the Tzemach Tzedek quotes the words of the Alshich,
he brings what is said in Likkutei Torah, beginning with "Mizmor Shir Chanukas HaBayis" 49,
that "mizmor" is the song of the angels and "shir" is the song of the souls.
And ostensibly, the intention is
that what the Alshich said — that "mizmor" refers to the first matter
(the abundance of blessings for Israel)
and "shir" refers to the second matter
("For You will judge the peoples with equity")
— is according to the homiletic approach
(and it is known 50
that the Arizal said about him that his soul was from the world of Drush [homiletics]),
but according to what is explained in Likkutei Torah
(which is founded on Kabbalah,
sod [mystical secret])
that "mizmor" is the song of the angels and "shir" is the song of the souls,
one must say
that "mizmor" relates to "For You will judge the peoples with equity,"
for the influence to the nations of the world comes from the angels
(through the seventy princes),
and "shir" relates to the influence that will be bestowed upon Israel.
And the Tzemach Tzedek continues in his notes,
that the reason we recite this psalm after the Counting of the Omer
is
because the matter of Sefiras HaOmer is the refinement of the seven attributes of the animal soul,
for the root of the animal soul is from the Chayos HaMerkavah — angels,
the matter of "mizmor,"
and through the refinement and elevation of the animal soul, there is also the elevation of the G-dly soul,
"shir."
And one could say
that this [reason] that we recite this psalm, which speaks about the matter of the refinement of the nations
(in their simple sense)
after the Counting of the Omer, whose matter is the refinement of the attributes of the animal soul
(within Israel),
is
because through the refinement of the attributes of the animal soul, the refinement of the nations is also drawn forth,
"For You will judge the peoples with equity."
And based on this, it is even more understood that on Erev Rosh Chodesh Iyar
(the month of Sefiras HaOmer)
the matter of the segulah [treasured quality] of "v’shilshis" [the third] is emphasized,
the refinement that refines "from all the nations" which brings about "you shall be to Me a segulah [treasured possession]."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that just as during the Omer the elevation of the animal soul (mizmor) leads to the elevation of the G-dly soul (shir), so too in the Messianic era, the sanctification of G-d's name through judging the nations will increase the flow to Israel, and the order of "mizmor shir" reflects this sequence even in that future time.

translations.translation: And behold, just as during the Counting of the Omer,
through the elevation of the animal soul
("mizmor")
the elevation of the G-dly soul is brought about
("shir"),
so too is it in the days of Mashiach
[for this psalm speaks primarily about the days of Mashiach],
that through His name being sanctified in the world
("For You will judge the peoples with equity"),
through this there will be an addition in the influence to Israel.
For although the matter of the refinements
(through which the revelation is drawn forth)
is now,
and the matter of the days of Mashiach is the drawing forth of the revelation that comes after the work of refinements,
nevertheless,
through "For You will judge the peoples with equity" and His name will be sanctified in the world then,
there will be an even greater addition in the drawing forth and revelation to Israel, relative to the drawing forth and revelation that will be then through the work of refinements now.
And therefore it says "mizmor shir,"
"mizmor" before "shir"
[although it speaks primarily about the days of Mashiach,
and the matter of "mizmor" is "For You will judge the peoples with equity" that will be then],
because even then there will first be "mizmor" and through it there will be
(an addition in)
"shir."
And this that in the verses
(after the first verse)
it says "May G-d be gracious to us and bless us" etc. before "You will judge the peoples with equity" etc.,
one could say
that since the purpose of creation is for the sake of Israel 51,
it is therefore understood
that the primary matter of the days of Mashiach is that then a great abundance will be bestowed
(in spirituality and in physicality)
upon Israel,
except that the perfection of the influence to Israel is through His name being sanctified in the world,
and therefore it says "May G-d be gracious to us and bless us, may He cause His face to shine upon us, Selah" before "You will judge the peoples with equity" etc.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains, by analogy to the soul and body, that the ultimate revelation achieved through serving G-d with Torah and mitzvos in a physical body will primarily be at the time of the Resurrection of the Dead, which is far superior even to the highest level of the Garden of Eden.

translations.translation: And along the lines of what is known regarding the matter of soul and body,

in addition to the fact that the G-dly revelation drawn to the soul through its service in Torah and mitzvos while clothed in a body is a revelation far superior to the revelation it had before its descent below,
nevertheless, the revelation that comes through the service of Torah and mitzvos in a physical body will primarily be at the time of the Resurrection of the Dead,
when the soul will be clothed in a physical body.
For although even the revelation in the Garden of Eden after the soul departs from the body is far superior to the revelation of the Garden of Eden that the soul had before its descent,
because the revelation of the Garden of Eden after its descent into a body and its departure from the body comes through the service of Torah and mitzvos in a physical body,
nevertheless,
the primary revelation that comes through the service of Torah and mitzvos will be at the Resurrection of the Dead,
when the soul will be clothed in a body 52.
And this is also understood from the matter of the Resurrection of the Dead itself,
that all of Israel will rise to life,
even the souls that have been in the Garden of Eden for several thousand years,
and three times each day they ascend to a more elevated level,
and nevertheless, in the future they will be clothed in bodies,
because the revelation of the World of Resurrection is far superior to the revelation of the Garden of Eden, even the most elevated level of the Garden of Eden 53.
